executive_preview: The clearest signal this week is a widening split in automotive electrification. Affordable EVs are moving closer to market in Europe and the United States, while premium brands are using electrification to increase performance and preserve brand identity. Nissan's reported Wave, Ford's Fathom and Slate target the affordability gap, but their commercial significance depends on whether manufacturers can deliver at scale and with acceptable equipment.

lead_development.title: Battery-health data is becoming commercially relevant to used-EV valuation
lead_development.what_happened: AVILOO's reported 500,000-plus tests found generally moderate degradation across 20 EV models, but meaningful differences by model. At 150,000 km, median battery health was reported at 90.32% for the Tesla Model Y, 88.94% for the Model 3, 93.79% for the Hyundai Ioniq 5 and 92.53% for the Mustang Mach-E.
lead_development.why_it_matters: Independent battery state-of-health measurement could reduce uncertainty in used-EV pricing, trade-in appraisal, warranty decisions and financing. The results also challenge the assumption that all EV batteries have similar residual performance.

signals.title: Tesla Begins Limited Public Cybercab Operations While Robotaxi Scale Remains Unproven
signals.teaser: Tesla opened public rides in its steering-wheel-free, pedal-free Cybercab in Austin.

signals.title: Affordable EV Competition Is Moving Toward a Sub-$30,000 Price Band
signals.teaser: Ford reaffirmed a 2027 launch for the Fathom electric midsize truck at a reported $28,350 starting price, Slate reportedly offered selected preorder customers December delivery windows at $26,400 including destination, and Nissan's reported Wave is targeted below €20,000 in Europe.

signals.title: Premium Automakers Are Using EVs to Increase Performance Rather Than Simply Replace Engines
signals.teaser: Bentley said its first EV, the Torcal, will be its most powerful and fastest-accelerating production model.

downside.title: Autonomous-driving liability and transparency exposure is increasing for Tesla and the wider ADAS market.
downside.teaser: Electrek and Yahoo Autos reported multiple fatal crashes in which Tesla data indicated driver-assistance engagement, alongside a confidential settlement that avoided a jury trial.

upside.title: Battery-health certification could improve used-EV appraisal and customer confidence.
upside.teaser: The AVILOO dataset demonstrates scalable battery state-of-health measurement across 500,000-plus tests.
